# Risk aggregation and option-pricing numerics

Economics: [fi-risk-dv01-and-transforms](../../fi-risk-dv01-and-transforms/SKILL.md),
[curve-pca-factor-model](../../curve-pca-factor-model/SKILL.md), [vol-rates-options-rv](../../vol-rates-options-rv/SKILL.md),
[stir-convexity-adjustment](../../stir-convexity-adjustment/SKILL.md). This file is the code-level contract and the fixtures.
Fixture signs: Darbyshire's books print positive pv01 for paid fixed; this repo uses positive for receive/long duration.

## Covariance, CoVaR, min-VaR, PCA
- Covariance from daily CHANGES in bp, never levels; >= 100 observations; horizon matched to the VaR horizon. `cov_bp` in the bundled script rejects shorter histories. (Darbyshire, Pricing and Trading IRD 3e, 2022, ch.14.) A printed snippet uses `diff(-1)*100`, which is sign-flipped versus `x_t - x_{t-1}`: harmless for covariance, wrong for signed P&L.
- `c = sqrt(S' Q S)`; `VaR_5% = 1.645 c` (book rounds 1.644), `VaR_1% = 2.326 c`; Euler (Aumann-Shapley) allocation `S_i (Q S)_i / c` sums to c; a negative allocation is a diversifier. Under normality `VaR_1% ~ ES_2.5%` (2.326 vs 2.338 sigma).
- Fixture: Q (bp^2) = [[8.7, 7.4, 5.1, 2.2], [7.4, 7.3, 4.7, 2.2], [5.1, 4.7, 4.9, 1.8], [2.2, 2.2, 1.8, 1.9]] on 2/5/10/30Y, S = (-10,000, 2,500, 10,000, -4,000) per bp. The book prints c = 16,174 (VaR 5% 26,590; 1% 37,620) from the unrounded covariance; the printed rounded matrix gives c = 16,402. The bundled selftest asserts 16,401.98 exactly (independent triple loop) and within 2% of the book. Do not claim to reproduce 16,174.
- Min-VaR trade in a subset `h` of instruments: `S_trade = -Q_hh^-1 (Q S)_h` (`np.linalg.solve`, not inverse), `S_new = S + S_trade`. Single-trade fixture (book): 2Y +2,948 cuts c by 15.6%; 5Y +2,304 by 7.7%; 10Y -475 by 0.2%; 30Y +3,373 by 4.1%. The rounded matrix gives +3,023 and -16.1% for the 2Y (exact: 26,300/8.7 and c 16,402 to 13,766). If the best single hedge cuts VaR only ~15%, the book is relative-value risk, not direction. Only one single-instrument trade at a time; at full size several can raise VaR, so trade about 50% and re-run.
- PCA: `E' Q E = diag(lambda)`; use eigh (symmetric), sort descending, fix signs by a deterministic rule (largest-|loading| positive), strip NaN/INF first, recompute big decompositions less often. PC multipliers are uncorrelated with variance = eigenvalue; dropping PCs understates variance (rescale). Correlation matrix to remove volatility scale; covariance to keep it. Smallest eigenvalue = minimum-variance combination (Quant Finance Stack Exchange, "Step-by-Step PCA algorithm", Jan 2014). Use non-centred multipliers for P&L attribution by PC.
- Fly weights from covariance (Quant Finance Stack Exchange, "How to adjust butterfly 2s5s10s swaps trade for directionality?", 2018, edited 2021): (a) PCA divide `w = [-1/e_2Y, 2/e_5Y, -1/e_10Y]` is sign- and scale-dependent (PC1 = [-1, 0, 1] gives [1, inf, -1]); (b) min-VaR with 5Y fixed at 2: `wings = -Q_ww^-1 Q_w5 x 2`; (c) minimum-variance least squares `beta = pinv(X) y` on daily changes, no intercept. EUR 2016 out-of-sample std (units not stated): PCA 0.869, min-VaR 0.763, MVLSR 0.761, raw 50/50 0.840.
- Walk-forward PCA (expanding window, backward-looking data only) vs full-sample PCA: if results differ materially you are trading the estimator (BofA Merrill Lynch Global Research, European Rates Viewpoint: Many EGBs, one simple value tool, 21 Mar 2018).
- Cross-gamma: second-order risks are linear in first-order forward-zero-coupon risks split into discounting, forecasting (non-compounded) and forecasting (compounded); par risks do not work directly (transform via Jacobians). Magnitude about 1e-4 of first-order per element, quadratic in grid size, can dominate in volatile periods (Darbyshire, PT3e, ch.21-22). Gamma P&L `0.5 x Gamma x dr^2`.

## Regularised least squares and solvers
- Ridge as augmented least squares: `X~ = [X/sigma; sqrt(Lambda)]`, `y~ = [y/sigma; 0]`; solve by QR (`X~ = QR`, `w = R^-1 Q' y~`), "the method of choice" at `O(N D^2)`; for D >> N take the thin SVD first (Murphy, Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective, 2012, s.7.5). `ridge_qr` in the bundled script is asserted equal to the normal equations and exact at lambda = 0. No intercept: centre X and y first. Standardise columns first or the penalty is unit-dependent.
- K-fold CV with contiguous (purged) blocks for time series, one-standard-error rule for lambda. Shuffled folds leak.

## Swaption pricing (normal, physically settled)
- `x = (F - K)/(sigma_N sqrt(T)/100)` with F, K in percent, sigma_N in bp: payer `= (F-K) Phi(x) + (sigma_N sqrt(T)/100) phi(x)`; receiver = payer - (F - K) (parity holds only for physical settlement); price is in percent of annuity, multiply by annuity to get currency. Log (Black): `x = (ln(F/K) + 0.5 s^2)/s`, `s = sigma_LN sqrt(T)`, payer `= F N(x) - K N(x - s)` (Darbyshire, PT3e, s.20.2).
- Fixtures: payer F 1.325, K 1.500, T 5, 52bp normal = 0.3816 (38.16bp); asserted in selftest, with parity and an implied-vol round trip. Receiver, F 2.80, K 3.10, T 0.25, 13% lognormal = 0.3048 (checked by hand). ATM normal premium `sigma_N sqrt(T)/(100 sqrt(2 pi))`; breakeven daily move `sqrt(2/pi) sigma_N/sqrt(252)` (zero P&L on an unhedged ATM straddle).
- Implied vol: Newton `sigma += (O_mkt - O(sigma))/vega`, start 20bp (or 20%), 2-4 iterations; clamp positive; raise after 50 iterations. Straddle is not handled by the script: use put-call parity per leg.
- Units trap: the book's vega and theta helpers are per rate-percent; multiply by 100 for per bp (printed dollar vega/theta look 100x small). Cross-check ATM vega ~ `sqrt(T) x 0.399 x pv01`. Delta of a payer at F 1.10, K 1.30, T 1, 50bp is `Phi(-0.4) = 0.3446` (checked), gamma `phi(-0.4)/0.5 = 0.737` per rate-percent.
- Log vol explodes near zero rates (0.2% rate, 20bp absolute vol: 100% log vol unshifted, 40% at 30bp shift, 20% at 80bp shift). Always store (distribution, shift, day count) with every vol.
- Forward vol: `sigma^2 = (t s_t^2 - f s_f^2)/(t - f)`; 2Y7Y 50bp and 1Y1Y7Y 44bp give 1Y7Y-in-1Y = 55.4bp (checked). Par-to-forward (1Y5Y5Y from 1Y5Y and 1Y10Y with annuity ratio L = 2.10, rho = 0.95, vols 39 and 59): `sigma^2 = ((1-L)s1)^2 + 2(1-L)L rho s1 s2 + (L s2)^2` = 84.2bp (checked); the source's "naive 50/50" figure of 79 is reproduced by L = 2, rho = 1 (2 x 59 - 39). Falls monotonically in rho.
- The book's cash-settled annuity formula is printed with ambiguous placement of f ("verify against the ISDA definition"); do not copy it.
- Short-rate trees (Hull, Options, Futures and Other Derivatives 9e, ch.31): trinomial `dR = sigma sqrt(3 dt)`, `j_max` = smallest integer > 0.184/(a dt), branching `pu = 1/6 + (a^2 j^2 dt^2 - a j dt)/2`, `pm = 2/3 - a^2 j^2 dt^2`, `pd = 1/6 + (a^2 j^2 dt^2 + a j dt)/2`. Test: 3Y put on a 9Y zero, K = 63, a = 0.1, sigma = 0.01: analytic 1.8093; trees with 10/100/500 steps 1.8468/1.8128/1.8091. A tree that fails to converge toward the analytic value as steps grow is wrong.

## Convexity code pattern
- Do not model futures-FRA convexity as margin reinvestment; it is a gamma effect. Expected convexity P&L `0.5 x Gamma x (sigma sqrt(T))^2`. Constant-gamma estimate 9.6bp on a hedged 1bn 2025 SOFR swap (Gamma 12.2 USD/bp, 139bp normal vol, 1.88y) overstates by ~60% versus linear gamma decay (about 6bp), because gamma falls to about 7.0 after a year (Quant Finance Stack Exchange, "Why are FRA/futures convexity adjustments necessary?", 2019, updated 27 Jul 2023).
- Calibration: fit a smooth parametric convexity curve (spline on a few nodes) to the most traded short swaps rather than a theoretical model; positioning, margin and CCP effects often dominate (Quant Finance Stack Exchange, "STIR Futures convexity adjustment", Jun 2025).
- Mids from several instruments: stack prices and spreads/flies as rows of `A p = s` and solve weighted least squares (weights 1 for outrights, 0.2 for spreads, 0.1 for the fly) instead of trusting a last-traded or single-book mid (Darbyshire, PT3e, ch.19).
